analysis.title: Situation Room: Into bonds and stocks
key_insights: US HG bond fund and ETF inflows were +$7.70bn in the week ending Nov 4, up from +$4.35bn the prior week. HG Funds took in +$1.59bn (biggest inflow in 9 weeks, from -$2.85bn) while HG ETF inflows slowed to +$6.11bn from +$7.20bn.
The HG inflow was boosted by the typically large fund inflows on the first day of the month. Excluding that, the weekly inflow was +$5.0bn, similar to the prior week.
Short-term HG inflows rose to +$1.29bn from +$0.30bn, and ex-short-term HG rose to +$6.40bn from +$4.05bn.
Equity fund inflows improved to +$29.54bn from +$14.54bn, and loan funds to +$0.13bn from -$0.31bn.
HY flows were roughly steady at +$1.55bn (from +$1.80bn). Muni inflows slowed to +$1.61bn from +$2.60bn, and global EM bond funds had outflows of -$0.47bn (from -$0.44bn).
Money market funds took in +$94.46bn last week after a -$11.36bn outflow the week before.

Year-to-date flows as of Nov 4: HG $416.3bn (8.2% of AUM), loans 9.1% of AUM ($16.2bn), munis 8.4% ($92.1bn), HY total 1.6% ($7.4bn), EM 2.9% ($25.9bn), money markets 2.7% ($225.8bn), equities 1.5% ($430.8bn), all fixed income 8.6% ($717.3bn). Loans have had the biggest inflows in 2026 so far, followed by munis.

US IG issuance was $22bn across 11 deals on the day, $74.9bn week-to-date and month-to-date. The average new issue concession was 12.2bps, and this week's new issues are trading 4bps tighter on average from pricing.

Oracle priced a five-tranche IG deal on Nov 2 totaling $10.0bn (3y to 20y) at spreads of 240-335bps, with 14-18bps concessions on the 3y to 10y tranches. Meta priced $15.0bn across five tranches on Nov 3 (5y to 30y) at spreads of 110-220bps, with new issue concessions of 32bps on the 5y and 7y, and 27bps on the 10y. Apple came with a multi-tranche deal on Nov 5 with spreads of 22-55bps.
BofA estimates IG dealer inventories of US issuer bonds rose to +$7.2bn on Nov 5 from -$5.0bn on Oct 28. Inventory DV01 rose to -$3.5mn from -$10.5mn.

Estimated net dealer buying in HG was $389mn on Nov 5, $10,598mn over the past week and $24,362mn over 4 weeks. By sector over 4 weeks, Banks/Brokers were +$6,976mn, Health Care +$4,108mn and Technology +$3,401mn. Utilities were -$316mn on the day.
Average daily HG fund and ETF inflow was $598mn in November so far, down from $708mn in October. Daily IG inflow was $1,000mn on Nov 4 versus -$1,270mn on Nov 3.
HG fund flows tend to follow returns since Oct 2023, but flows have been decoupled from returns since around Oct 2024.

Foreign demand proxies for USD IG: net dealer volume before 8am ET (1-10yr) was -$90mn on Nov 5 vs -$195mn the day prior. Dealer-to-affiliate 8am-noon volume was -$57mn (1-10yr) and -$39mn (10yr+). The 12-day MA of foreign buying rose $14mn over 5 business days while the 30yr Treasury yield was unchanged.

Exhibit 26 text: net foreign buying of 10yr+ IG bonds follows changes in Treasury yields, a drop in yield typically leads to lower foreign demand. 12-day MA foreign buy rose $14mn over 5 business days ending Nov 5 while the T yield change was 0bps.
vol_and_positioning: Equity fund inflows doubled week over week to +$29.54bn, while money market funds took in +$94.46bn, after a -$11.36bn outflow the prior week.
Cumulative 2-year flows as of Nov 4 are 26% of AUM for HG, 10% for HY and 8% for loans.
